subject: Urban Planning
title: Inclusionary Zoning: Building Equity Into Code
description: A short lesson to help you apply Inclusionary Zoning: Building Equity Into Code.

hook.text: New York requires developers building over 10 units to make 20-30% of them permanently affordable. It's zoning as social policy.

buildup.text: Mandatory inclusionary zoning ties affordable housing to market-rate development. No public funding needed.

discovery.text: Developers accept inclusionary rules in exchange for density bonuses — more floors mean more profit, even with affordable units.

twist.text: If the requirement is too high, developers stop building. If too low, too few affordable units result. Calibration matters.

climax.text: Over 1,000 US jurisdictions use some form of inclusionary zoning. The debate is about percentages, not principles.

punchline.text: Build luxury. Include affordability. Let the market fund the mix.

quiz.question: What incentive do developers receive in exchange for inclusionary zoning requirements?
options: Tax-free status for the first ten years of operation
Density bonuses allowing them to build more floors and units
Free land from the city government for construction
